questions.question: If x + y = 6, find the value of x³ + y³ + 18xy.
questions.questionHtml: If x + y = 6, find the value of x³ + y³ + 18xy.
questions.solution:
Use the identity:

x³ + y³ = (x + y)³ − 3xy(x + y)

Substitute x + y = 6:

x³ + y³ = 6³ − 3xy · 6 = 216 − 18xy

x³ + y³ + 18xy = (216 − 18xy) + 18xy

= 216

questions.solution:

questions.question: In a certain code language, ‘MARKET’ is written as ‘NBSLFU’ and ‘SCHOOL’ is written as ‘TDIPPM’. How will ‘GARDEN’ be written in that language?
questions.questionHtml: In a certain code language, ‘MARKET’ is written as ‘NBSLFU’ and ‘SCHOOL’ is written as ‘TDIPPM’. How will ‘GARDEN’ be written in that language?
questions.solution:
Explanation:

• Each letter of the word is replaced by the next letter in the English alphabetical order.
• Example:
– MARKET → NBSLFU
M→N, A→B, R→S, K→L, E→F, T→U
– SCHOOL → TDIPPM
S→T, C→D, H→I, O→P, O→P, L→M

• Applying the same logic to GARDEN:
G→H, A→B, R→S, D→E, E→F, N→O

• Hence, GARDEN → HBSEFO

Correct Answer: D

questions.question: Read the given statement and conclusions carefully. Decide which of the given conclusions is/are definitely true from the statement. Statement: P ≥ R < T ≤ S = Q > M Conclusions: I. P > M II. Q ≥ T
questions.questionHtml:
Read the given statement and conclusions carefully. Decide which of the given conclusions is/are definitely true from the statement.

Statement:
P ≥ R < T ≤ S = Q > M

Conclusions:
I. P > M
II. Q ≥ T

options.text: Both Conclusion I and Conclusion II are true
options.html: Both Conclusion I and Conclusion II are true

options.text: Neither Conclusion I nor Conclusion II is true
options.html: Neither Conclusion I nor Conclusion II is true

questions.solution:
Explanation:

• From the statement: P ≥ R < T ≤ S = Q > M
This means S = Q and Q > M, so S > M and Q > M.

• Conclusion I: P > M
There is no direct relation between P and M (P is only related to R).
Hence, Conclusion I is not definitely true.

• Conclusion II: Q ≥ T
From T ≤ S and S = Q, we get T ≤ Q, which means Q ≥ T.
Hence, Conclusion II is definitely true.

Correct Answer: A) Only Conclusion II is true

questions.question: Read the following passage and answer the given questions accordingly: Marine archaeology is often a race against time and nature. The deep-sea environment, while preserving artifacts in low-oxygen "anoxic" zones, is increasingly threatened by bottom trawling and climate change. Ocean acidification is dissolving the calcium carbonate in ancient shipwrecks, effectively erasing history before it can be charted. Recently, the discovery of the Endurance in the Antarctic highlighted the benefits of frigid temperatures in preventing wood-eating worms from destroying hulls. Yet, the cost of such expeditions remains prohibitive, often leaving these sites vulnerable to "salvage hunters" rather than scientific researchers. Q- Why was the Endurance shipwreck so well-preserved?

Q- Why was the Endurance shipwreck so well-preserved?

options.text: Because it was made of reinforced steel.

questions.solution:

The frigid Antarctic temperatures prevent wood-eating worms from surviving, which helped keep the Endurance shipwreck exceptionally well-preserved.

This (3) _____, though ostensibly prudent, begets collateral inefficiencies—inventory bloat and logistical (4) _____. Ultimately, deglobalization's panacea proves a (5) ______ pyrrhic victory. Q- What will come in blank (3)?
questions.questionHtml:
In the following passage some words have been omitted. Fill in the blanks with appropriate words accordingly:

Geopolitical realignments have (1) _____ tectonic shifts in global supply chains, compelling multinationals to (2) _____ from just-in-time to resilient architectures. This (3) _____, though ostensibly prudent, begets collateral inefficiencies—inventory bloat and logistical (4) _____. Ultimately, deglobalization's panacea proves a (5) ______ pyrrhic victory.

Q- What will come in blank (3)?
questions.solution:
✅ Correct Answer

Blank (3) should be realignment (पुनः संरेखण / पुनः व्यवस्था).

Catalyst (प्रेरक / उत्प्रेरक): Refers to something that triggers change. But here, the sentence is describing the shift itself, not an external trigger. “Catalyst” doesn’t fit naturally.

Panacea (सर्वरोगनाशक): Means a cure-all solution. Doesn’t fit because the sentence is about inefficiencies, not solutions.

Aberration (विचलन / असामान्यता): Means deviation or abnormality. Doesn’t align with “ostensibly prudent” (seemingly wise).

Realignment (पुनः संरेखण / पुनः व्यवस्था): Perfect fit. The passage began with “Geopolitical realignments…” and now continues logically: “This realignment, though ostensibly prudent, begets collateral inefficiencies…” It directly refers to the strategic shift being prudent but costly.

questions.question: Ustad Asad Ali Khan was a legendary maestro associated with which of the following stringed instruments?
questions.questionHtml: Ustad Asad Ali Khan was a legendary maestro associated with which of the following stringed instruments?
questions.solution:
✅ Correct Answer: Rudra Veena

Explanation

Ustad Asad Ali Khan was one of the last great exponents of the Rudra Veena, an ancient stringed instrument deeply associated with the Dhrupad tradition of Indian classical music. He belonged to the Khandar school of Dhrupad and dedicated his life to preserving and performing on this rare instrument, known for its deep, meditative resonance. His contribution was widely recognized, and he was honored with the Padma Bhushan for his artistry.
